title: Delhi Sultanate
capsule: The Delhi Sultanate was established in 1206 when Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a former Ghurid general, founded the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty at Delhi after his masters' conquests of northwestern India. Under Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296–1316) it reached its greatest territorial extent, projecting power deep into the Deccan and repulsing two Mongol invasions; Muhammad bin Tughluq (r. 1324–1351) made an ill-fated attempt to shift the capital to Daulatabad and lost control of the Deccan. Timur's sack of Delhi in 1398 devastated the sultanate beyond recovery; the Lodi dynasty (1451–1526) briefly revived Delhi's power before Ibrahim Lodi fell to Babur at the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526, founding the Mughal Empire. The dataset's terminal date of 1529 reflects the persistence of minor Lodi resistance until Babur's defeat of the Afghan coalition at the Battle of Ghaghra.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core northern territories are well documented through sultanate chronicles and numismatic evidence; Deccan and southern frontier zones are less precisely mapped and varied seasonally with campaigns.
